claim: Kyoto now has six three-Michelin-starred restaurants as of the 2026 guide
quote: Gourmet capital Kyoto now has six three-Michelin-starred restaurants

claim: Miyamaso received three Michelin stars in 2026, the first new three-star restaurant in Kyoto in six years
quote: A New Three-MICHELIN-Star Restaurant Shines in Kyoto for the First Time in Six Years

claim: Gion Sasaki, Hyotei, Isshisoden Nakamura, and Kikunoi Honten have maintained three stars consistently since 2021
Miyamaso is an inn and restaurant with over 120 years of history, nestled in the Hanase mountains
quote: an inn and restaurant with over 120 years of history, nestled in the lush Hanase mountains on the fringes of Kyoto

claim: Miyamaso received one star in 2010, two stars in 2011, and three stars in 2026
quote: first awarded one star in 2010 and held two stars since 2011 before being promoted to three stars in 2026

claim: Mizai charges ¥60,000 per person, accepts cash only, allows no food photography, and was booked 13 months in advance by the reviewer
quote: Price: ¥60,000 per person for the tasting menu... Cash only... No photos of food allowed

claim: Mizai is considered by some critics as the finest of all Japan's Michelin-starred restaurants, with a single evening seating at 6pm
quote: considered by some critics as the finest of all Japan's Michelin starred restaurants

claim: Mizai's chef is Hitoshi Ishihara; the restaurant is nearly impossible to book even 18 months in advance through luxury hotel concierges
quote: even with 18 months' notice through The Ritz Carlton concierge, the response was 'that could be tricky'

claim: Hyotei is a 450-year-old kaiseki restaurant near Nanzenji Temple with signature dishes including Hyotei Tamago and seasonal porridges, bookable online 90 days in advance
quote: a long history, starting about 450 years ago as a tea house

claim: Hyotei is at 35 Kusagawa-cho, Nanzen-ji, Sakyo-ku; 10-minute walk from Keage Station; closed 2nd and 4th Tuesdays
quote: Closed 2nd and 4th Tuesday of a month (Main building)

claim: Hyotei dinner tasting menu runs ¥25,000–35,000 per person; run by the 15th generation of the owning family
quote: decide between 25000, 30000 and 35000 yen... run by the 15th generation of the owning family

claim: Kikunoi Honten is in Higashiyama Ward, run by third-generation chef Yoshihiro Murata who advocates for washoku as UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage; uses historic well water from the 1500s
quote: Third-generation owner Mr. Murata, known for advocating Japanese cuisine as UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage... uses historic well water sourced since the 1500s

claim: Kikunoi Honten dinner courses: Dinner B ¥47,500, Dinner C ¥60,500, Kikunoi Special ¥74,000 per person
quote: Dinner B course at 47,500 yen per person, Dinner C course at 60,500 yen per person, Kikunoi Special course at 74,000 yen per person

claim: Isshisoden Nakamura is at 136 Matsushitacho, Nakagyo-ku; 5-min walk from Karasuma Oike Station; lunch Wed/Sat only; prepayment required; private rooms only; no children under 12
quote: 5-minute walk from subway Karasuma Oike station

claim: Miyamaso is at 375 Hanaseharachichō, Sakyo-ku; dining ¥28,000–33,880 per person; overnight ¥70,000–88,550 per person including dinner and breakfast; reachable via Kyoto Bus Route 32 (~1h40m)
quote: Dining: ¥28,000–¥33,880 per person... Overnight Stay: ¥70,000–¥88,550 per person (includes dinner and breakfast)

claim: Gion Sasaki charges ¥31,000 for lunch and ¥54,000 for dinner per person (includes ¥8,000 booking fee); closed Sundays; dinner from 18:30
quote: Lunch: ¥31,000 per person (includes ¥8,000 booking fee). Dinner: ¥54,000 per person (includes ¥8,000 booking fee)

claim: Chef Hiroshi Sasaki installed a brick oven in a renovated 90-year-old wooden house; the dining experience is theatrical with the goal being that guests leave saying how 'fun' it was
quote: Combining Sasaki's wealth of experience with the youthful sensitivity of his disciples... suffusing classic Japanese cuisine with fresh technique and imagination
